source: Durian Orchard (ការដាំធូរេន), by Vann Thana Busab and Montry Vong Phanith, published by the Northwest Cambodia Provinces Fruit Culture Development Committee (Battambang), 1998, 59pp, AIDOC code 178-001
text:
Durian needs a hot, humid tropical climate. Recommended growing conditions are roughly 25-30 degrees Celsius with air humidity around 75-80%. If growing in an area with distinct dry and wet seasons or with strong seasonal wind, growers should plant windbreak trees around the plot, since durian trees are easily damaged by strong wind, drop their leaves under sustained dry heat, and do not fruit well when repeatedly stressed by wind and drought.

Durian tolerates several soil types: clay loam, sandy clay loam (best, because it drains well and does not stay waterlogged), and lateritic/gravelly soil, provided the soil pH is in the range of 5.5-6.5. If the planting site has a shallow water table, growers should raise planting mounds and dig drainage canals to keep excess water away from the roots; standing water at the root zone is one of the most common causes of root and collar disease in durian.
